title: Associativity of ideal-power multiplication
statement:
For a quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$, the canonical
maps $\mathcal I^m\otimes\mathcal I^n\to\mathcal I^{m+n}$ are associative
and have $\mathcal I^0=\mathcal O_X$ as a two-sided unit.

proof.text: Write $\mu_{m,n}:\mathcal I^m\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal I^n\to\mathcal I^{m+n}$ for the canonical multiplication, with $m,n\in\mathbf N$. Fix any affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and put $J=\mathcal I(U)$. The definition of ideal powers gives quasi-coherence of every $\mathcal I^r$, $\mathcal I^r(U)=J^r$, and $J^0=A$. The affine tensor comparison is the canonical map sending $x\otimes y$ to its pure tensor section; it is bijective. Applied twice it also identifies sections of either triple tensor with the corresponding iterated module tensor, since the intermediate tensor sheaf is quasi-coherent by the same cited result. Under these comparisons, $\mu_{m,n}(U)$ is $x\otimes y\mapsto xy\in J^{m+n}$: the product of the two sections in $\mathcal O_X(U)$ lands in that ideal because $J^mJ^n=J^{m+n}$. This bilinear pairing determines the linear map by the module tensor universal property.

proof.text: For $m,n,k\in\mathbf N$, identify the target powers using $(m+n)+k=m+(n+k)$. On $U$, the canonical tensor associator $\alpha$ sends $(x\otimes y)\otimes z$ to $x\otimes(y\otimes z)$: bilinear extension gives this map and the inverse regrouping, whose composites are the identity on pure tensors and hence everywhere. The affine tensor comparisons of step 1 send these generators to the identical pure tensor sections, so they identify this map with the sheaf associator. The two sides of the required equation $\mu_{m+n,k}\circ(\mu_{m,n}\otimes1)=\mu_{m,n+k}\circ(1\otimes\mu_{n,k})\circ\alpha$ send $(x\otimes y)\otimes z$ to $(xy)z$ and $x(yz)$. These agree by associativity in $A$, and equality in the ideal follows from equality in $A$. The tensor product is generated by pure tensors; applying that fact twice shows that these triple pure tensors generate the whole source. Linearity therefore gives equality on all its sections over $U$.

source.place: Proof, affine calculation; expanded using Stacks Tags 01I8 (schemes-lemma-widetilde-constructions), 01CA (modules-section-tensor-product), and 00CX (algebra-lemma-tensor-product)

proof.text: For the left unit, $\mathcal I^0(U)=A$ and $J^{0+n}=J^n$. The map $\mu_{0,n}(U)$ sends $a\otimes y$ to $ay$, exactly the left unitor $A\otimes_AJ^n\to J^n$. Its inverse is $y\mapsto1\otimes y$: the two composites are the identity, since $1y=y$ and $1\otimes ay=a\otimes y$ by the balancing relation. For the right unit, $J^{n+0}=J^n$ and $\mu_{n,0}(U)$ sends $y\otimes a$ to $ya=ay$, exactly the right unitor $J^n\otimes_A A\to J^n$. Its inverse is $y\mapsto y\otimes1$, since $(ya)\otimes1=y\otimes a$. Generation by pure tensors extends these identities to all sections. The affine tensor comparisons send each displayed pure tensor to its pure tensor section, so the comparisons with the sheaf unitors are the same maps. Thus both unit equations hold over every affine $U$.

source.place: Proof, affine calculation; expanded using Stacks Tags 01I8 (schemes-lemma-widetilde-constructions), 01CA (modules-section-tensor-product), and 00CX (algebra-lemma-tensor-product)

proof.text: The formulas above commute with restriction. For nested affine opens $V\subseteq U$, restriction of ideal sections is induced by the ring restriction $\rho:\mathcal O_X(U)\to\mathcal O_X(V)$; hence $\rho(xy)=\rho(x)\rho(y)$ and $\rho(1)=1$. Tensor restriction sends $x\otimes y$ to $\rho(x)\otimes\rho(y)$, so multiplication, regrouping, and both unit formulas commute with it, first on pure tensors and then by linearity. In particular on a principal open $D(f)$ the multiplication formula is $(x/f^r)(y/f^s)=xy/f^{r+s}$; associativity gives $(xy)z/f^{r+s+t}=x(yz)/f^{r+s+t}$. This is the localization compatibility asserted in the blueprint, without any assumption that a tensor multiplication map is injective.

source.place: Proof, affine calculation; expanded using Stacks Tags 01I8 (schemes-lemma-widetilde-constructions), 01CA (modules-section-tensor-product), and 00CX (algebra-lemma-tensor-product)

proof.text: For each of the three equations, let $p,q$ be its two sheaf morphisms with the same source and target, after the indicated degree identifications and associator or unitor. They agree on sections over every affine open by steps 2 and 3. Given any open $W\subseteq X$ and any source section $s$ over $W$, cover $W$ by affine opens $V\subseteq W$, using the affine-basis lemma. Naturality gives $p_W(s)|_V=p_V(s|_V)=q_V(s|_V)=q_W(s)|_V$. The uniqueness part of the target's sheaf axiom gives $p_W(s)=q_W(s)$, so $p=q$. This proves associativity and both unit laws globally. No intersection of two affine opens is assumed affine: when needed the same affine basis refines their intersection.

blueprint_update.statement:
For a quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$, the canonical
maps $\mathcal I^m\otimes\mathcal I^n\to\mathcal I^{m+n}$ are associative
and have $\mathcal I^0=\mathcal O_X$ as a two-sided unit.

proof.text:
On an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ these maps are induced by
multiplication of the ideals $I^m$ and $I^n$ in $A$. Associativity and the
unit law are therefore the corresponding ring identities. Localization
preserves these identities, and equality of morphisms of quasi-coherent
sheaves can be checked on an affine cover, so the identities glue on $X$.
